subject: The command controller's per-frame update 0071F290 as a complete rule table, the consumers of the permission bytes +3Ch/+3Dh/+220h..+223h, 00721A40 whole with its two command entry paths, 00720180 whole, the owner of 009F6AD0 and the two Lua fire-target tails.
reuses: include/bsp/command_execution.hpp for the controller offsets and CommandSlot; include/bsp/director_target_gate.hpp for update_auto_target_hold and command_category_owns_fire_target

answer.question: 0071F290 as a per-frame rule table.
answer.result: Seven arms in a fixed order. (1) 0071F294-0071F2C1 abandons the frame unless the session object at +34h exists and reads set/clear/clear/clear at +5Ch/+5Dh/+60h/+5Eh. (2) 0071F2C7-0071F2F7 stores the shared default vector 00F87574/78/7C into path object 0's +30h/+34h/+38h. (3) 0071F2F8-0071F316 is the hold countdown of docs/DIRECTOR_TARGET_GATE.md. (4) 0071F317-0071F329 promotes mode 0 to 1 when queue slot 0 is occupied. (5) 0071F32A-0071F34E and (6) 0071F34F-0071F372 each ask vtable[78h] to begin one command (0 the override, 1 the queue head) while that command exists and has not accepted its target; a refusal raises that command's stage to the terminal 2 through 0071D9E0 or 0071D810. (7) 0071F373-0071F39F returns when the session mode at *(00E188A8)+1FE4h is 2, else ticks [+38h]->vtable[4](frameDelta) and then vtable[7Ch](). On the director those last two are 009F5DA0, the bot fire-target think, and 00836920 BSP_WeaponDirector_Step. So the update is the whole per-frame driver, not a timer with extras.

answer.question: The consumers of +3Ch, +3Dh, +220h, +221h, +222h and what each permission gates.
answer.result: The four enables have recovered names from the reflection visitor 008360C0: +220h artilleryEnabled, +221h aaEnabled, +222h torpedoEnabled, +223h depthChargeEnabled; +238h fireTargetID and +23Ch fireTargetIsPrimary come from the same visitor. Consumers: 0080DC70 reads both stance bytes as one predicate (two call sites, 008171F6 and 009F83CB); 009F5610 BSP_WeaponDirector_AutoTargetEnabled reads +3Dh allowMove plus slot 0's category; 008624C0 mirrors all six into a weapon panel and is the only consumer that says what they gate, allowFire being the master switch over a twelve-byte per-weapon enable array and each named enable going to its own setter; 009F1BC0 caches the four enables into the ship-AI record at +12B8h..+12BBh; 00720450 copies the two stance bytes controller-to-controller; the network snapshot pair 00721280/007214C0 writes all six into a message and 00721890/00721980/007219C0 writes the four enables back; 008FFA20 reads only +221h. The gun-bot doc's 'artillery flag' at +221h is the anti-aircraft enable.

answer.question: 00721A40 whole and the two entry paths 0071E7F0 / 0071ECF0.
answer.result: Seven IsA arms, 5Ah through 60h, behind an entry gate that needs [[director+34h]->vtable[13Ch]()]+5Eh clear. The 5Eh arm closes docs/WEAPON_DIRECTOR.md's open question about who writes +238h: 00721BF1 calls 00836240 BSP_WeaponDirector_StoreFireTarget, which stores at [ESI+14h] with ESI = this+224h, which is why a scan for a +238h displacement missed it. 0071E7F0 is the receive side of the override: a no-op guard, a 0071D6D0 validity test, a queue veto that refuses while slot 0 holds a category 1 or 2 command, then the record copy and mode = 2 with both override accepted and stage cleared. 0071ECF0 is the send side of the queue path and differs only by the message flag 1 that 00721A40 branches on at 00721B36.

answer.question: 00720180 whole.
answer.result: __thiscall(this)(owner) -> this, RET 4 at 00720440, body 00720180-00720442, one SEH frame. The session endpoint is owner[+28h], not the argument itself (0072020B/00720219). It zeroes both stance bytes, sets all four weapon enables to 1, seeds +1CCh with 1FFh, fills twenty dwords at +1D0h..+21Fh with D01502F9h (a block docs/WEAPON_DIRECTOR.md's field table did not have), memsets the ten command slots, initialises the previous-command and override records, and allocates the ten 50h-byte path objects into the pointer array at +1A4h.

answer.question: What holds 009F6AD0's address.
answer.result: Nothing. A scan of the whole file on disk for the little-endian dword and for every E8/E9 displacement resolving to it returns zero hits, so it is in no vtable, jump table or function-pointer table. It belongs to a family: the seven accessors at 00720D80-00720E0A and the six at 00861970-008619C6 are equally unreferenced, all on the same class. Whose this it takes cannot be settled from a call site; the controller reading is favoured because 00720D80 is the byte-for-byte same access on the controller and because the auto-target object's own +3Ch is a float set to FLT_MAX at 009F6AA8, which makes a byte compare against zero meaningless. Provisional.

answer.question: The two Lua tails.
answer.result: 0089C360 GetFireTarget: director->vtable[2Ch]() is the fire target; null pushes nil, otherwise the decimal form of the target's u16 id at +174h keys into the literal 'thisTable' and that value is pushed, then the temporary string block is returned to the sized storage pool. 0089A8B0 SetFireTarget: after the three argument branches it takes the director through vtable[114h] and calls 00835860(target, 1). The force argument is the constant 1, so a script set always wins over fireTargetIsPrimary while the network path can be refused. Neither tail pushes anything beyond that, so SetFireTarget returns zero Lua results.
